annotation.title_clean: House Bill No. 11366: An Act Regulating the Possession and Operation of Unmanned Systems, Providing Penalties for Violations Thereof, and for Other Purposes (Unmanned Systems Regulation and Safety Act of 2026)
annotation.title_en: House Bill No. 11366: An Act Regulating the Possession and Operation of Unmanned Systems, Providing Penalties for Violations Thereof, and for Other Purposes (Unmanned Systems Regulation and Safety Act of 2026)
annotation.authors_or_issuer: House of Representatives of the Philippines (Rep. Antonio T. Kho; Rep. Elisa T. Kho)
named_instruments_referenced: CAAP Civil Aviation Regulations Part 11 and 14
annotation.summary_en: Philippine House Bill 11366 proposes the Unmanned Systems Regulation and Safety Act of 2026, regulating aerial, ground and maritime unmanned systems through weight and risk classification, mandatory registry, operator licensing, dealer accreditation, no-fly zones, privacy protections, a weaponization ban, counter-drone powers, an inter-agency council and heavy penalties.
key_provisions_or_claims: Creates Inter-Agency Council on Unmanned Systems chaired by DOTr and a national registry of unmanned systems.
Classifies drones by weight (four categories) and operational risk (three classes); mandatory registration and operator licensing.
Prohibits weaponization, unlawful surveillance, hacking/spoofing, and flights near airports and critical infrastructure.
Authorizes PNP/AFP enforcement, grounding, seizure and counter-drone measures.
Sets fines and imprisonment up to reclusión perpetua, and treats drone use as an aggravating circumstance.
